title: Monsoon Fury Batters Gujarat: One Dead, Over 1,200 Rescued as South Gujarat Drowns
excerpt: Kaprada in Valsad records 16 inches of rain in 24 hours as rivers breach danger marks, hundreds of roads close, and NDRF teams scramble across the state's flood-ravaged south.
body:
• One person has died in Tapi district due to severe monsoon rains in south Gujarat.
  • Over 1,200 individuals have been rescued from flooded areas, particularly in Valsad, Navsari, Surat, and Tapi districts.
  • Kaprada taluka recorded the highest rainfall with 16 inches in a single day, leading to significant flooding.
  • Multiple rivers have breached danger levels, prompting evacuations and alerts for riverside villages.

Relentless monsoon rains have unleashed devastation across south Gujarat, killing at least one person in Tapi district and forcing the rescue of more than 1,200 others as rivers swelled past danger marks and entire neighborhoods went underwater, according to NDTV and The Hindu.

The worst-hit areas span Valsad, Navsari, Surat, and Tapi districts, where a 24-hour deluge ending on July 22 dumped rainfall measured in feet rather than inches. Kaprada taluka in Valsad recorded the highest single-day total at a staggering 16 inches (397mm), while Nanapondha registered 11 inches, according to the State Emergency Operations Centre (SEOC).

A Parking Lot Turned Lake

Viral footage from Valsad showed more than 50 cars submerged in a flooded parking lot, a scene NDTV described as emblematic of the monsoon's fury. In Navsari's Vansda taluka, an Eeco van attempting to cross the Bopi–Mola Amba causeway was swept away by strong currents, though its lone occupant was pulled to safety.

https://x.com/tv9gujarati/status/2079943839792652546

Near Nanapondha, 16 passengers aboard a private bus stranded in rising floodwaters were rescued by local police and volunteer swimmers. In Valsad city, more than 200 residents of Kashmir Nagar were evacuated to a nearby primary school after the Auranga River burst its banks, reaching 4.5 meters near the Bhairavi Bridge.

"Drainage pumps installed at vulnerable locations have helped bring waterlogging under control, while Quick Response Teams have been deployed across all 13 municipal wards to respond to emergencies."

— Jayesh Upadhyay, Navsari Municipal Commissioner

Rivers Breach, Roads Vanish

Multiple rivers across the region have breached or are nearing danger levels. The Kaveri River at Bilimora crossed the 20-foot mark—one foot above its danger threshold—forcing the district administration to put 30 riverside villages on alert. Navsari Collector Manish Gurwani confirmed that two SDRF teams had been deployed to Bilimora, with 45 people rescued so far.

The infrastructure toll has been staggering. Valsad district alone has shut 284 roads, while Navsari closed 132 roads and an additional 71 within the city, according to Bhaskar English. Railway services were disrupted as the Sayajinagari Express was cancelled and the Mumbai–Ahmedabad Double Decker Express was short-terminated at Navsari station.

In Surat, the Bhedwad creek crossed its danger level of 6.75 meters, reaching 6.90 meters and flooding low-lying neighborhoods. Schools across Surat and Navsari were closed. The Surat Municipal Commissioner ordered evacuations from the Sanjay Nagar slum area near the creek.

Massive Rescue Operation

Authorities have mounted one of the largest monsoon rescue operations in recent years. A total of 33 disaster response teams—13 from the NDRF and 20 from the SDRF—have been deployed across rain-hit regions, according to the SEOC. Additional teams were called into Surat overnight, with fire brigade units equipped with boats stationed at vulnerable points including Limbayat, Puna Patiya, and the Dindoli Road creek bridge.

In Navsari, a 24-hour control room is monitoring the situation through digital surveillance and CCTV cameras, with field teams sending real-time updates via WhatsApp.

"We have repeatedly raised the issue with the authorities over the years but no permanent solution has been implemented to address the recurring flooding."

— Kalpesh Patel, Navsari resident

What Diaspora Families Should Know

The monsoon crisis coincides with a period when many NRIs visit family in Gujarat. Flight and train services to the region have been disrupted, and district administrations are urging residents to avoid all unnecessary travel. Those with family in south Gujarat—particularly in Valsad, Navsari, Surat, and Tapi—should check in regularly as connectivity remains patchy in flooded areas.

More Rain Ahead

The India Meteorological Department has maintained its red alert for Navsari and Valsad, warning of continued extremely heavy rainfall through July 24. The system is expected to shift northward, with extremely heavy rainfall forecast for Sabarkantha and Aravalli districts on July 25 and 26. Ahmedabad may also see rain spells in the coming days.

With reservoirs filling rapidly and major rivers already above danger marks, officials are bracing for the possibility of further flooding across the state.
